name: Flood risk standing advice for local planning authorities
fact: Environment Agency standing advice updated 28 May 2026 sets when site-specific flood risk assessments and agency consultation are required across Flood Zones and surface-water/critical-drainage contexts.
gate: Standing advice is a screening/decision framework, not a parcel-specific FRA or planning approval.

name: Preparing a flood risk assessment standing advice
fact: Current standing advice explains the evidence expected in site-specific FRAs and the need to consider present and future flood risk from relevant sources.
gate: An FRA prepared to guidance is not automatically accepted and does not itself grant planning permission.

name: Flood risk assessment: Flood Zones 1, 2, 3 and 3b
fact: Current guidance distinguishes Flood Zones 1, 2, 3 and functional floodplain 3b and explains sequential-test and assessment expectations.
gate: Flood Zone 3 is not automatically Flood Zone 3b; the current local SFRA is needed for functional-floodplain evidence.

name: Flood risk assessments: applying for planning permission
fact: Guidance updated 28 May 2026 requires site-specific assessment of relevant current and future flood sources and review of model information where needed.
gate: National map/model data does not replace a proposal-specific FRA, levels, access and mitigation evidence.

name: Flood map for planning service
fact: The Environment Agency planning service provides location-based flood-zone and climate-change screening and states its maps/data are not guaranteed to be error free.
gate: A service result is screening evidence and not a planning decision, exact survey or site-specific hydraulic model.

name: Understanding and using the updated surface water flood risk map
fact: Environment Agency guidance explains national/local-model surface-water risk mapping, likelihood bands, depth and hazard information and limitations.
gate: Surface-water mapping is probabilistic planning evidence, not a forecast that a particular property will flood in a specific event.

name: Strategic flood risk assessment guide for planning authorities
fact: SFRA guidance requires authorities to assess all relevant sources of flooding, climate change, functional floodplain and local evidence.
gate: An SFRA is strategic evidence and cannot replace site-specific FRA evidence for a development parcel.

name: Flood risk and coastal change planning practice guidance
fact: Planning practice guidance covers sequential/exception tests, site-specific FRA, functional floodplain, climate change, coastal change and watercourse controls.
gate: Passing a sequential or exception test is not planning permission and does not discharge separate flood permits or consents.

name: Check the long term flood risk for an area in England
fact: The official service covers river/sea, surface-water, reservoir and available groundwater risk and explicitly does not say whether an individual property will flood.
gate: Area risk must not be converted into certainty for an exact building or parcel.

name: Flood risk assessments: climate change allowances
fact: Environment Agency climate-change allowance guidance sets the uplifts and scenarios used in flood-risk assessment for future rainfall, river flow and sea level.
gate: An allowance is an assessment input, not a mapped future flood boundary or guaranteed event magnitude.

name: Water storage areas dataset
fact: Environment Agency water-storage-area mapping identifies areas used to store floodwater and notes that flood-risk management assets do not remove all risk.
gate: Storage/defence presence is not proof a parcel is protected from overtopping, failure or residual flooding.

name: Reservoir flood maps: when and how to use them
fact: Reservoir guidance explains modelled credible worst-case extents and how the maps support emergency/planning understanding.
gate: Reservoir flood-map presence does not state dam-failure probability and must not be used alone to determine development outcome.

name: Flood risk maps for surface water: how to use the map
fact: Environment Agency guidance explains surface-water likelihood, depth, speed and hazard layers and their planning/emergency uses.
gate: Mapped likelihood/hazard is modelled risk, not measured flood depth at an exact parcel.

name: Planning Data flood risk zone dataset
fact: Planning Data reports a large authoritative flood-risk-zone dataset, but its collector/new-data dates are substantially older than the current Environment Agency planning map.
gate: Use current Environment Agency flood-map evidence for live screening; platform collector age must not be mistaken for current flood-zone state.

name: Planning Data flood risk level dataset
fact: Planning Data defines controlled flood-risk-level categories but the taxonomy itself contains no parcel-specific hydraulic evidence.
gate: A controlled level code is schema semantics and not a site-specific flood-risk conclusion.

name: National standards for sustainable drainage systems
fact: National SuDS standards set design principles for runoff quantity, water quality, amenity/biodiversity and exceedance/extreme rainfall.
gate: Designing to a standard is not approval, adoption or proof the site's drainage outfall/capacity is secured.

name: Groundwater source protection zones
fact: Environment Agency SPZ guidance defines zones around drinking-water sources according to travel time and pollution risk.
gate: SPZ presence is a groundwater-protection screening constraint, not evidence of contamination or available abstraction capacity.

name: Groundwater vulnerability 100k legacy dataset
fact: The legacy 1:100,000 groundwater-vulnerability mapping remains published but is based on older source information and newer Environment Agency vulnerability products are available.
gate: Do not prefer legacy vulnerability classes over current datasets for a parcel assessment.

name: Groundwater vulnerability data England
fact: Current Environment Agency groundwater-vulnerability mapping classifies aquifer vulnerability to pollutants released at ground level.
gate: Vulnerability is susceptibility, not observed groundwater contamination or a water-quality measurement.

name: Groundwater vulnerability maps 2017
fact: Environment Agency specialist groundwater-vulnerability mapping provides national/regional screening at mapped scale.
gate: Mapped class cannot replace site hydrogeology, borehole data or contaminant-pathway assessment.

name: Groundwater flooding susceptibility
fact: Environment Agency groundwater-flooding susceptibility data is a broad hazard/susceptibility product intended for strategic use rather than exact property risk.
gate: Susceptibility is not likelihood or a prediction that a target property will flood.

name: Groundwater protection guidance collection
fact: Environment Agency groundwater-protection collection brings together position statements, pollution controls, abstraction and related guidance.
gate: A guidance collection is not a site-specific permit, licence or water-quality result.

name: Groundwater protection position statements
fact: Environment Agency groundwater-protection position statements set its regulatory approach and note that the document is under review following regulatory changes.
gate: Policy position is not a site decision; current permit/licence and local hydrogeology still control.

name: Protect groundwater and prevent groundwater pollution
fact: Groundwater protection guidance separates discharge permitting/exemptions from abstraction controls and site hydrogeological risk.
gate: A lawful discharge route does not grant abstraction rights, and an abstraction licence does not authorise pollution.

name: Investigate a groundwater source
fact: Environment Agency guidance updated 29 April 2026 explains when consent is needed to construct/test a borehole or well before a groundwater abstraction application.
gate: Consent to investigate a source is not an abstraction licence and does not guarantee a sustainable yield.

name: Check if you need a licence to abstract water
fact: Current guidance explains abstraction licensing thresholds and that groundwater investigation consent can be required before abstraction licensing.
gate: A threshold check or exemption does not establish aquifer capacity or planning suitability.
